text:
Alex: quick check — noticed a weird spike in the Q1 dashboard from the benchmark webinar on 3/18. sessions +3.2k but only ~120 MQLs. figures look off? :thinking:
Morgan: saw that too. GA4 shows sessions up but conversions flat. could be UTM mismatch or form debounce issue.
Priya: I pulled form logs — inbound hits from the webinar landing page are there but a bunch are missing a utm_medium param. looks like some registrants clicked an email with stripped params.
Sam: hmm that would break attribution but not the lead capture itself. question: are we displaying last-touch on the dashboard?
Alex: dashboard uses last_non_direct by default. but our weekly report used first-touch last week for the benchmark narrative. probably a mismatch between dashboards and the slide deck.
Jamie: yeah that's classic. we should standardize the reporting view — either pick one and surface it everywhere or show both.
Morgan: agree. quick win: add a small note row on the dashboard explaining attribution window + model. second, can we run a re-attribution for that webinar to align with the slide deck?
Priya: I can re-run attribution on the leads table. SQL I used to check mediums:
```
SELECT utm_source, utm_medium, COUNT(*) as leads
FROM aggregated_leads
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-03-17' AND '2026-03-19'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY leads DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Sam: thanks — also check for duplicate query params like utm_medium=\"email\" vs utm_medium=null. We had the same in last quarter.
Alex: action items: Priya re-attribute & share counts (ETA today), Morgan add dashboard note + v2 widget for both models (ETA EOD), Sam to scan the email templates for param stripping, I'll update the benchmark slides if numbers change.
Jamie: for the weekly KPI review tomorrow let's include a tiny row showing model delta (first vs last) so we don't get surprised again. :+1:
Priya: starting re-run now, will drop results in this thread when done.
Morgan: if re-attr shows a >10% swing we should call it out in the exec notes.
Alex: agreed. thanks team — keep it short in thread. :raised_hands:
